claims.text: Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a balance between a composition-dependent thermodynamic driving force for ordering and a diffusion-related kinetic barrier.
The high-temperature BCC phase of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 becomes thermodynamically unstable at lower temperatures.
Al lowers the free energy of an ordered phase such as B2 or a related ordered variant relative to the BCC state.
Transformation to the ordered state occurs only when atomic mobility is sufficient for the ordering reaction.
Slow furnace cooling permits more atomic diffusion than rapid quenching.
Rapid quenching kinetically suppresses diffusion relative to slow furnace cooling.
Atomic mobility becomes limiting across the proposed transition region from above 1000°C to below 900°C.
Short-range ordered clusters or embryonic ordered precipitates mediate transformation from the BCC phase.
The mediating ordered domains may be B2-type.
At moderate temperatures, the free-energy difference between metastable BCC and the ordered phase becomes significant.
Slow cooling provides sufficient diffusion to overcome kinetic barriers and permit ordering.
Rapid quenching preserves the high-temperature BCC state at lower temperatures despite its proposed thermodynamic instability.
Slow-cooled samples will develop a measurable volume fraction of an ordered secondary phase within the BCC matrix.
Rapidly quenched samples will largely retain the BCC structure.
The ordered-phase fraction will be greater after slow cooling than after rapid quenching.
The proposed behavior is limited to cooling conditions that distinguish diffusion-enabled from diffusion-limited regimes.
